name: 1936 Prairie Avenue — the Thompson/Allerton house (Italianate, L. B. Dixon, 1869-70)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '2½S.B.; bay4B; rear2B brick dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

built.note: The Chicago Tribune of 30 October 1869 describes the house 'now building' and intends 'to erect the walls and enclose the building the coming year, and finish off the subsequent year'; the Tribune of 30 March 1879 reports its sale to Samuel W. Allerton.

research_note: Refined from the district draft (T-2329) in place by T-1901 (piece 1), under the draft's own id, as a K01 Italianate house: Daniel M. Thompson's 1869-70 villa by L. B. Dixon, Samuel W. Allerton's from 1879 and still his family's in 1904, razed 1915. The sheet 28 census (ruling r28-allerton) reads the 1911 label as '1918' over '(1936)', so this drawn house IS the Allerton house and the bare 1936 corner is its lawn; there is no second villa and no house at 1916 or 1930. Built from the 1911 sheet's plan (s28fp-1918-b1), the Chicago Tribune's description of 30 October 1869 (chicago_tribune_1869_10_30_thompson_residence: its sizes, storey heights, materials and rooms) and the undated winter photograph Chicagology reproduces (chicagology_1936_prairie_exterior_photo), whose camera is solved in data/reference_views/house_1918_prairie/. What is reconstructed is listed under liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901.

documented_range.note: The 1904 target to the 1911 sheet that draws the house: built 1869-70 (Tribune), the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped), and it was razed in 1915 after the Hump Hairpin Company bought it in 1912.

position.symbolic_location: 1918 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1918 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).
position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 28.500, v 1.000 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation -0.628 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main block on the 1911 sheet (trace s28fp-1918-b1), u from its rear wall to the north block's face (17.7 m; the front's south part stands 0.95 m behind it, under the verandah), v from the south wall between the dining range and the reception bay (v 0) to the north wall (15.8). The Tribune's 'extreme size' is 66 ft 6 in by 94 ft; the sheet's, with the bays, the tower and the rear range, about 18.7 by 29.2 m.

stories.note: '2½S.B.' on the 1911 sheet: two full storeys over a raised basement and a half storey. The 1869 Tribune: 'an attic in the main house, which is lighted by frieze-light windows'; built as a short third storey whose lights stand in the frieze under the cornice, as the photograph shows them on the south flank.

construction.note: The 1869 Tribune: the basement 'faced with ashlar of Connecticut brown stone, from the Portland quarries ... 6 feet high, with heavy moulded base and water-table'; 'all exterior walls above the basement are faced with the best quality of Baltimore pressed brick'; 'all the windows are trimmed with brown stone'. The 1911 sheet colours the house brick; the Tribune of 9 January 1898 calls it 'his big red brick house'.

principal_floor_m.note: The 1869 Tribune: 'The main floor is six feet above the grade line' (1.83 m); 'the windows for basement are entirely above ground'. Written while the house was building; the photograph's basement storey under the principal floor's sills agrees.

storey_heights_m.note: The 1869 Tribune: principal story 14 ft 9 in (4.50 m), second story 13 ft 6 in (4.11 m) for the main part; the main building 44 ft (13.41 m) from grade to the top of its cornice. The attic storey, 3.32 m, carries the wall head to 13.76 m, so that K10's bracketed cornice, whose crown stands 0.37 m under the wall head, tops at 13.39 m, the Tribune's 13.41 (T-3330: at 2.1 m the crown stood at 12.19 m, 1.2 m short; the photograph, read down the tower's front on one vertical scale, puts the main cornice's top at 0.60 of the tower's height, as the Tribune's 44 and 73 ft do).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: The brick walls over the basement; the Tribune gives the rubble wall to grade as 25 inches and an air space of four inches inside the brick, not the brick's own thickness. K01's top of range.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: As the front: every exterior wall is the same pressed brick over the same ashlar basement (Tribune 1869).

service_wall_brick.note: Every exterior wall above the basement is Baltimore pressed brick (Tribune 1869) and the house was 'his big red brick house' (Tribune 1898), so the flanks and rear are laid in the kit's red-brown panel as the front is; K03 has no smooth pressed panel, so its rough red-brown stands for it (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901).

stone_front.note: The 1869 Tribune: the ashlar of Portland brownstone, 'rubbed surface, with square rustic joints', 6 ft high with a heavy moulded base and water-table, under the pressed brick; brownstone trim. The photograph shows the pale stone basement storey under the darker brick (y 870-965 px at the south-east corner).

side_base.note: The brownstone ashlar runs round the flanks to the main floor's level (Tribune 1869: 'the foundation of all exterior walls ... faced with ashlar'); the photograph shows it along the south flank.

street_front_brick.note: Baltimore pressed brick over the ashlar (Tribune 1869), red (Tribune 1898); the kit's red-brown panel (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901).

street_front_trim.note: Every window 'trimmed with brown stone' (Tribune 1869): the photograph's heavy moulded hoods over the principal and chamber windows, plain heads on the frieze lights. T-3370 (eleventh pass): the chamber storey's front lights, over the verandah and north of the tower (x about 1450-1820 px, y 480-560), stand under tall carved hoods whose tops the print draws crested with raised scrolled carving, the hood and its crest rising about 1.0 m over the lights' heads (the hood band at y about 520-535 px over heads at 540, the crest's top at about 500); each cornice-hood lintel on that storey carries K09's carved crest (`crest`, the T-3270 palmette between two volutes) 1.0 m wide and 0.5 m high. The principal storey's lights stand behind the verandah, where no picture shows their heads, and keep the plain hood. The crest's carving is the kit's (the print resolves only a raised scrolled block over each hood); its sizes are reconstructed off the print (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901).

wall_head.note: A deep cornice on paired scrolled brackets round the house, the attic's frieze lights between them, in the photograph (y 395-450 px at the south-east corner); its top near 13.4 m, the Tribune's 44 ft. T-3397: its paint read off the photograph's tones (the method of docs/RESEARCH/colour-1700-block-T-3244): the belvedere's corona prints near black (median 0-30 of 255 across x 1525-1700, y 88-100 px) beside its own red pressed-brick walls at 96-120 (x 1545-1665, y 150-260), and the main cornice's corona and frieze at the south-east corner 41-99 (x 1010-1110, y 393-413) against the flank's brick at 172-184; a vertical face under the same overcast sky as the walls, so the dark is its paint, not a shadow. Pressed red brick already prints dark on a blue- or ortho-sensitive plate (K03's red-brown 0.197, 0.098, 0.068 gives 0.088 ortho); the kit's tan timber (0.27, 0.24, 0.20) would print lighter than the brick, so the cornice and the belvedere's are painted a dark brown (0.06, 0.045, 0.035; 0.042 ortho), as the brownstone-coloured cornices of the period were. The hue is reconstructed (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901).

roof_form.note: A low hipped roof behind the cornice with a railed deck, in the photograph (the rail at y 260-300 px over the south-east corner).

roof_pitch_deg.note: The photograph's hip slopes, low behind the cornice.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's reach past the wall in the photograph, about 0.75 m.

roof_covering.note: The 1869 Tribune: 'The roof will be covered with slate, with copper flashings'. The kit's slate cuts are laid only at 45 degrees and over, and the photograph's hip is low, so the hip is covered in the kit's painted standing seam (as 1906's) with the Tribune's copper flashings; the slate is listed under liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901.

hip_deck.note: The hip cut off at a deck with a rail round it, in the photograph (y 260-300 px over the south-east corner, about 2.5 m over the cornice's top through the camera); K01's hip deck with 1906's pierced rail. Raised with the main cornice by T-3330, 15.0 to 16.22 m. T-3370 reads it on the photograph's re-solved camera (data/reference_views/house_1918_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): the rail's top over the deck's south-east corner (x 1345, y 257 px) stands at about 17.0 m, where the build's (16.22 m deck, 0.8 m rail) stands, so its height is kept; its corner reads about 0.5-1 m west and south of the build's. T-3370 (fourth pass): the photograph's rail runs from the deck's south-east corner (x 1345, y 257 px) west along the south side and passes behind the right stack (x 1228-1285), and does not come out west of it: there (x 1150-1225) the hip's pale slope rises to the stack with no rail on it. So the rail ends at u 8.3 (rail.from_u_m), where the south rail's line passes behind the stack through the camera (x 1255 px), closed by a cross-run that the camera puts behind the south rail's own panel; west of it the deck's edge is a curb, the rail's plinth. Where the deck itself ends west of the rail the photograph cannot say (it sees no deck surface from the street), so the hip's level cut is kept; liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-stage-3370. T-3370 (seventh pass): the photograph's rail turns its south-east corner at x 1345 px, y 257 and its east run ends at a post at x 1405-1418, y 280-300, past which the print shows sky where the build's rail ran on to x 1505; the hip's north-east line falls away from the post's foot (x 1420, y 300). Through the committed camera at the rail's top (17.02 m) the south-east corner reads at u 11.29 on the south rail's line (v 5.38) and the post's outer face at v 8.2 on the east rail's line, so the deck's east edge stands at u 11.4 and its north edge at v 8.2 (edges_m), not the uniform 25 deg cut's 12.42 and 10.52: the east face pitched about 21.7 deg and the north about 18.6 deg from the hip's eave line, the south and west faces kept at 25. The deck's north-east corner then projects to x 1421, y 302, where the print's hip line starts; liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-deck-3370.

window_kit.note: Two-light sashes with a meeting rail in the photograph's windows.

stair_tread_m.note: The stoop's treads; the photograph shows the flight end on.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The landing at the stoop's head, as deep as the columned porch over it is out.

stoop_width_m.note: The flight under the columned porch, about as wide as the porch's span in the photograph.

entrance_bay.note: The 1869 Tribune: 'The main entrance is through a tower', approached 'up a flight of stone steps, which is covered by a stone porch, with fluted stone Corinthian columns'. T-3367 cuts the door in the tower's face (the tower carries the entrance, as T-1881's forward block does), at s 8.65, 1.1 m in from its north corner: the photograph draws the porch under the tower's north part (x about 1690-1815 px) and the shaft plain south of it (x about 1600-1690 px); liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901. T-3370: with the tower moved to v 7.95-11.75 (see the bays' note) the door stands at s 10.65.

front_bays.note: The 1869 Tribune: the reception room (south of the hall) has 'two windows in the east front' under the verandah (s 1.8, 4.0); the parlor (north of it) 'is lighted by two windows on the east front' (s 13.4, 14.7); the main entrance 'through a tower' (s 8.65, in the tower's face, T-3367). Places along the front read against the 1911 sheet's tower (v 5.95-9.74). T-3370: the door moves with the tower to s 10.65, still 1.1 m in from its north corner, the photograph's porch hood spanning about s 8.6-11.9 through the re-solved camera.

sash_by_storey.note: Tall principal-floor windows, chamber windows a little shorter, and the attic's 'frieze-light windows' (Tribune 1869), low horizontal lights under the cornice, in the photograph's south flank (y 455-470 px). The frieze lights stand 1.72 m over the attic's floor, under the brackets (T-3330, with the attic raised to the Tribune's cornice).

basement_lights.note: 'The windows for basement are entirely above ground' (Tribune 1869), in the ashlar under the principal windows.

side_bays.note: The south wall between the dining room's range and the reception room's bay: the 1869 Tribune's side entrance on the south, 'lighted by a large window opening to the south' (s 9.85 of the 1.6 m the sheet leaves there). The bays' own lights are theirs.

north_bays.note: The parlor's north wall; no picture shows the north flank.

rear_bays.note: The library's two west windows (Tribune 1869) where the rear wall stands clear of the rear range (v 14.2); the second is the octagonal bay's.

chimneys.note: Tall corniced stacks over the roof in the photograph: one over the south flank's rear part (x 905-995 px) and one over its front part (x 1215-1290 px); the third, on the north side, is reconstructed. T-3370 places the two south stacks on the photograph's re-solved camera (data/reference_views/house_1918_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): held on the line v 0.9 the photograph's left stack (x 905-995 px) stands at u 1.7, over the flank's west end, not u 6.0 (about 125 px east of it in the photograph), and the right one (x 1215-1300 px) at u 11.7 (from 12.5; the final fit reads it at 12.3, the two fits' spread). Their tops read about 17.4 and 18.2 m on that line, the build's within about 0.9 m and 0.1 m; the stack right of the tower in the photograph (x 1820-1860 px) stands, through that camera, in front of the house's line, so it is the neighbour's, not this house's north stack. T-3370 (second pass) reads the two stacks' heights and heads through the same camera, at about 39 px a metre on the left one and 42 on the right: the left one's top stands at y 270 px, 17.33 m (built 18.22, so about 35 px high), so it stands at its own 17.35 m (a hip's stack read off a picture may, as a mansard's does, clearing the hip's covering under it by 0.6 m); the right one's top at y 185 px, 18.26 m, the build's 18.22. Each carries a heavy moulded head over a stone band: the left one's head y 270-305 px (16.43-17.33 m, about 0.9 m) standing about 12 px (0.3 m) out each side of its 65 px shaft, its band at y 318 (16.09 m, 1.7 m over the roof under it); the right one's band at y 267 (16.29 m), under it a sunk panel to y 303 (15.43 m) on its east face. So the three are dressed from the K15 kit's panelled form (chimneys.k15, k15.stack.sherman, without its corbel blocks, which the print does not resolve): its two stone bands 0.55 and 1.75 m over the roof under each stack, a sunk panel 0.45 m wide on the street and rear faces from 1.0 m over that roof to 1.08 m under the head (the right one's 15.37-16.29 m, the photograph's 15.43-16.29), the left one plain (its shaft under the head is too short for one and the print shows none), and a head of three corbelled courses (0.15, 0.15 and 0.2 m, out 0.06, 0.13 and 0.2 m) under a stone cap 0.35 m thick and 0.28 m out, 0.85 m in all, for the print's 0.9 m and 0.3 m. Courses and cap are read at the print's scale, not measured, so reconstructed (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901). Still open: the right one's head is two-staged in the print, a broad moulded cap at 16.75-17.3 m with a narrower stage on it to the top at 18.26 m, where the build's one 0.85 m head stands at its top; and the left one's shaft reads about 65 px across where the build's 1.1 by 0.8 m stack spans 52 px, about 0.25 m broader, within the print's blur. T-3370 (fourth pass) builds the right stack's head as the print draws it (x 1215-1302, y 185-260 px, about 42 px a metre): the K15 head's corbels and broad cap stand lower, to 17.30 m (the print's broad moulded cap, y 225-248, 16.75-17.30 m), and on the cap a narrower stage (k15 stage) to the top at 18.22 m (the print's 18.26): a brick block 0.58 m high about the shaft's own width (x 1232-1285 against the shaft's 1228-1285, so 0.05 m in) under its own 0.34 m stone cap 0.1 m out (y 185-200), with the dark opening the print shows in its east face (x 1267-1282, y 203-215: about 0.36 m square) sunk 0.15 m into each broad face; its sunk panel stands 0.38 m under the lowered head (panel_under_head_m), so it runs from 1.0 m over the roof to just under the upper band, where the print draws it (to y 303, 15.43 m, under the band at y 267). The stack is moved to u 12.3, this camera's own reading of it (the committed fit; u 11.7 was the first fit's), which puts its shaft at x 1226-1283 for the print's 1228-1285. The stage's and vent's sizes are read off a blurred print and its sunk vent on the rear face is the street face's mirrored; liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-stage-3370. T-3370 (seventh pass): the reconstructed north stack stood at u 9.0, v 14.9, which the committed camera draws at x 1490-1535 px, y 263 against the print's open sky right of the deck's rail, so the photograph says no stack stood there; it is moved to u 14.0, where the camera puts it (x 1638-1691 px, y 241) behind the tower's belvedere (the print's x 1530-1744, the render's 1617-1754), so the print can neither show it nor rule it out. Its place stays reconstructed; liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-deck-3370.

rainwater.note: Copper gutters ('copper flashings', Tribune 1869) behind the cornice and two downpipes at the rear; no picture shows them.

entrance_kit.note: The 1869 Tribune: the steps 'covered by a stone porch, with fluted stone Corinthian columns, and from these columns spring stone brackets, which support a Corinthian cornice of stone'; the photograph shows that porch's columns under the tower's north part and its flight running north along the front from it (x 1655-1950, y 700-960 px). K07's door under 1906's columned hood stands for it, on the tower's face (T-3367); its landing runs along the face under the hood (v 7.55-9.75) and the flight leaves its north end parallel to the front (a side stoop, T-2530's), down to the walk. The fluting and capitals are T-1902's. T-3370: the landing moves with the door and the tower, to v 9.55-11.75. T-3370 (thirteenth pass): the porch's balcony as the photograph draws it over the columns (x 1690-1820 px): its cornice's foot at y about 693 px and its railing's top at about 650, level with the foot of the dressing room's pair over it (sill 7.08 m), where the build's hood hung its soffit at 5.2 m (y 730) under a 0.5 m fascia, so the porch stood about 0.85 m lower and squatter than the print's. The soffit rises to 6.0 m over a 0.2 m fascia and a 0.2 m cornice, the deck at 6.4 m, about the chamber floor's (6.33), and the railing 0.65 m high to 7.05 m, just under the pair's sills; its balusters and rail in the front's trim stone, pale as the print's over the porch's stone (reconstructed off the print, liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901).

corner_porch.note: The 1869 Tribune: the reception room's front windows 'are shaded by a verandah, with stone floor, Corinthian fluted columns, and stone cornice and roof', and the chamber over it opens 'on to the roof of verandah, which forms a balcony, with stone railing and stone balusters around it'. The 1911 sheet draws it south of the tower (s28fp-1918-b1 p2, v about 0-5.9, out to u 18.56); the photograph shows three openings and the balustrade over them (x 1380-1600 px). T-3356 stands the front's two piers between the arches as the photograph's columns (x 1487-1505 and 1555-1568 px, between the openings' 45-50 px; capitals at y 708-722 px): fluted shafts 0.32 m across at the foot on the 0.4 m piers, each on a square plinth and a torus, under a capital of two flaring tiers and a square abacus at the springing. The end piers stay solid, as the photograph shows them. The leafage is a few pixels across in the print; the tiers stand for it (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901). T-3357 sets an iron rail across the three front openings: the photograph's dark bar across their feet (y 822 px, about 0.8 m over the floor on the openings' 45-50 px to their 1.2 m span) and the dark standard under it in the middle of the first two (x about 1460 and 1527 px; the third opening is in shadow), built as a 0.06 m square bar from jamb to column at 0.8 m on one 0.06 m standard an opening. Its section is a few pixels in the print and its iron is the dark tone's reading (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901). T-3370 sets its place along the front on the photograph's re-solved camera (data/reference_views/house_1918_prairie/chicagology_photo.json): it runs from the house's south-east corner (the photograph's x 1421 px, under the main cornice's nearest corner) to the tower's south face (x 1643 px), about 8 m, with its two columns at x 1493 and 1557 px about 2.55 m apart: so three openings of 1.9 m on 2.3 m centres, its columns at s 2.63 and 4.93, between the kit's 0.5 m end piers (s 0-7.6, stopping 0.35 m short of the tower as before), where the 1911 sheet's porch strip gave 5.6 m and 1.2 m openings. The reception room's two front windows (s 1.8, 4.0) stay in the first two openings, where the photograph shows light through them. T-3370 (thirteenth pass): the balcony over it as the photograph draws it (x about 1420-1640 px, y 635-700): a pale moulded balustrade (y 635-670 px, about 0.8 m on the verandah's 43.5 px a metre) over a cornice (y 670-680) carried on a row of modillions, pale blocks with dark gaps about 0.4 m apart along the front (y 680-698), hanging down to the arches' crowns. Built so: the entablature's soffit lowered from 6.33 to 6.2 m, its cornice 0.22 m deep standing 0.3 m proud on modillions 0.12 m wide, 0.15 m out from the face and hanging 0.25 m to the crowns (5.95 m), at about 0.42 m centres (so the gaps between them stay open to the print's oblique view, as its dark gaps are), and the balustrade 0.8 m high, so its rail tops at 7.22 m where it had stood at 7.78, about 0.6 m over the print's; the cornice, its modillions and the balustrade laid in the front's trim stone, the dressings' own (the Tribune's 'stone cornice' and 'stone railing and stone balusters'), as the print draws them pale in the window hoods' tone over the arcade's walls. The modillions' size and spacing and the mouldings' depths are read off a few pixels of the print, so reconstructed (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901).

windows.why_not_ordinary: the 1869 Tribune's dressing room in the tower, 'lighted by two windows over main entrance': paired over the door (T-3367), as the photograph draws two lights over the porch. T-3370 (eleventh pass): the photograph draws the pair over the porch under heavy carved hoods crested as the front's chamber lights are (x about 1690-1810 px, y 500-540): each light in a moulded brownstone surround (K08's T-2931 jambs 0.1 m broad, as the pair's narrow pier between them allows, under a 0.25 m head 0.12 m proud) with K09's carved crest on its head, 0.9 m wide; T-3370 (twelfth pass): the print's hoods and crests rise about 1.15 m over the lights' heads (the left crest's top at about y 510 px over heads near 555, on the tower front's 39.6 px a metre), up into the blind stage over the storey, so each surround's head is the deep hood K08 allows (0.4 m) and its crest 0.6 m high is let past the storey's band (crest.past_band, as K08's scrolled pediment may rise; the blind stage over it has no light for it to reach), hood and crest about 1.0 m over the heads where they had stopped at 0.57 m under the band (sizes reconstructed off the print, liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901)

the belvedere's tall round-headed lights, one to a face, in the photograph (y 200-280 px; the arched heads at x 1595-1625, T-3318); T-3397: each framed as the photograph frames it, in an arched surround about 2 m across on its 3.8 m face (x 1565-1645 px against the face's 1530-1680): the K08 architrave at its widest, 0.45 m, on imposts under a keystone. T-3370: the belvedere stands square and clear over the roof (the tower's whole stage), so its south face, lit beside the front in the photograph with its arched frame, is the front's width and framed as the front is; the north and west faces, which no picture shows, are lit and framed alike (inferred: a belvedere is lit to every side) T-3370 (ninth pass): the arched frame's colonnettes, a slender shaft each side of the surround from the sill to the springing (x about 1561-1566 and 1631-1638 px on the south face, 6-8 px, about 0.2 m on the face's 35 px a metre), built as K08's architrave columns, 0.16 m square on a base under a capital, carrying its imposts; their leafage and mouldings are finer than the print's pixels (liberty L-k01-1936-allerton-1901)

the reception room's half-octagonal stone bay 'having a southern exposure' (Tribune 1869); two lights in its front, 1.9 m apart, as the photograph draws a pair to each storey on that face (x 1220-1315 px, T-3370)
